command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
base=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)
outside=$({ git diff --name-only "$base"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | grep -v "^$change/" | grep -vxF "$record" | grep -v '^\.gnomish-task/' || true)
[ -z "$outside" ] || { echo "$outside"; echo "the specify stage writes only under $change/ and $record - if you made the edits above, undo each of them yourself with: git checkout $base -- <file>; other active changes are someone else's work and stay exactly as they are"; exit 1; }

findings.message: tasks.md promises 'File size: every file stays under 200 lines' and .claude/rules/process-invariants.md says 'Target 100–200 lines per file; 300 is a hard cap', but tasks add scenarios and tests to files already at or over the limit, with no split task: src/test/features/app_shell/steps/app_shell_notices.steps.ts is 273 lines and task 7.3 adds 4 scenarios plus an onRegisteredSW fake registration (very likely >300); src/views/shared/LocationRow.test.tsx is already 224 lines and gains a UX3 test (4.3); app_shell_smoke_e2e.steps.ts (199, task 8.2), locationsReorderE2eHelpers.ts (196, task 6.5), LocationList.test.tsx (196, task 6.4), time_selection_select_time.steps.tsx (190, task 6.3) and locations_reorder_drag_e2e.steps.ts (188, task 6.5) all receive new code. Add split or extract steps to the tasks (for example a new *_legacy steps or test file per feature) so an implementer can meet the stated limit.

Task 6.5 puts emulateEngineWithoutPointerEvents into src/test/features/locations/steps/locationsReorderE2eHelpers.ts (196 lines, a locations-specific helper), yet tasks 6.6 (time_selection) and 10.2 (browser_compatibility) also use it. Put the shared E2E helper in its own module (for example under src/test/) so other feature folders do not import from locations step internals and the file stays under the size limit.

Task 6.1 / design D8 add a minimal PointerEvent class extending MouseEvent to src/test/setup.ts, but an equivalent stand-in already exists: src/views/shared/dayTrackFixture.tsx:33-47 has 'class FakePointerEvent extends MouseEvent' and useFakePointerEvents(), which calls vi.stubGlobal("PointerEvent", FakePointerEvent). The design does not mention it. Either move the existing FakePointerEvent into setup.ts and drop the per-file stub, or state how the two coexist, so the stand-in has one owner.

Glossary owner not updated: docs/glossary/time.md:11 defines **Legacy zone name** with '*Code:* `virtual:time-zone-aliases`, `canonicalizeTimeZoneId`'. Task 5.1 adds getLegacyZoneNames (canonical → legacy names) for that same concept, but handoff H3 (task 11.3) only adds new terms and never adds getLegacyZoneNames to that entry. .claude/rules/glossary.md requires: 'A change that shifts a term's meaning, owner or Russian name updates the entry in the same change.'

findings.message: Task 5.4 (and the mutation run in 5.7 and the FR2 legacy-boot scenarios in 10.1) import `src/lib/legacy/installLegacySupport.ts`, which imports `virtual:legacy-core-js`, but task 5.6 registers the plugin that serves it only in `vite.config.ts`. `packages/client/vitest.config.ts` has `plugins: [react(), zoneDataPlugin()]` and no task adds `legacyCoreJsPlugin` there or aliases the module, so the virtual import cannot resolve under Vitest/Stryker and design D11 ('jsdom tests ... re-import the module under test') does not hold as planned. Add a task step that registers the plugin (or an alias/mock) in vitest.config.ts.

FR12 / the browser-compatibility scenario 'Full height has a fallback' (every `dvh` height preceded by a `vh` fallback) has no lasting automated test or CI check: only task 8.1 verifies it by inspecting the build once, and the `check:legacy-build` script of D9 / task 9.1 checks only `inset:`. This breaks M1 ('100% of FR1–FR13 ... have at least one automated test or CI check') and .claude/rules/test-planning.md ('Every FR/NFR/UX from proposal must have at least one automated test covering it'). Add a rule to findLegacySyntaxIssues/check-legacy-build (or a unit test over the Tailwind output) that fails when a `dvh` declaration lacks a preceding `vh` fallback, with its it.each case.

findings.message: FR4 (proposal) requires resolving a wall-clock time in a renamed zone 'with every disambiguation (UNIQUE, GAP, AMBIGUOUS as in ADR-0003)', and the task requires the spike to cover PlainDateTime#toZonedDateTime with disambiguation. But the spike (tasks.md 1.1, design D4) and the browser-compatibility scenario 'A wall-clock time in a renamed zone' only test UNIQUE (2026-03-08T10:00) and GAP (2026-03-29T03:30). No task or scenario tests an AMBIGUOUS Kyiv time (e.g. 2026-10-25T03:30, the fall-back), which is the earlier/later path resolveWallClock uses (src/model/wallClock.ts:32-33). Add an AMBIGUOUS row to the spike, the spec outline and the 10.1 feature.

Tasks 1.1, 5.1 and 10.1 and design D11 rely on 'vi.resetModules() and import @/lib/temporal ... fresh' to make temporal-polyfill load again and capture a fake Intl.DateTimeFormat. But src/test/setup.ts already imports systemClock from @/lib/temporal, and vitest.config.ts has no test.server.deps.inline entry for temporal-polyfill. Vitest does not reload packages from node_modules that it leaves to Node, so the polyfill keeps the real constructor, which accepts Europe/Kyiv in Node. The spike's checks (09:30 +02:00, UNIQUE, GAP) would then pass without the fake rejection or the retry ever running. The tasks must inline temporal-polyfill for these tests, or assert that the fake native constructor was called and rejected Europe/Kyiv, so the spike can tell 'shim reached' from 'shim bypassed'.

Task 7.3 drives the 'A check on return fails offline' scenario with failUpdateCheck from src/test/fakeServiceWorker.ts. That helper passes onRegisteredSW a registration whose update() always rejects, and usePwaUpdateStatus already runs update() on registration ('registration?.update().catch(() => setIsUpdateCheckFailed(true))'). So the start-up check sets the failure note before the page becomes visible again, and the scenario passes without the recheck in FR10. The task should specify a registration whose start-up update() resolves and whose later update() rejects, and assert that the note is absent before the visibility change.
